transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-06-11 15:00 UTC, duration 47m, attendees listed above.

Summary: quick renewal/checkin to align on retainer uplift, APAC/Japan onboarding and a short on-prem pilot ask from the platform team. Discussed burst billing, SLA, and next steps for procurement.

Topics: Retainer uplift options; Multi-region activation (Japan + EU); On-prem pilot / VPC + KMS; Benchmark plan and timeline; Contract amendment and procurement steps.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Alex Mercer: hey everyone thanks for hopping on, um we wanted to use this slot to go through the retainer uplift and make sure the japan region plan fits with your rollout, mike?
[00:12] Michael Tran: yeah thanks alex, appreciate it. We're looking at a sustained uptick through q3—peak windows during campaign pushes—so want a predictable base and a burst band. procurement/ana's on the call to understand financials.
[00:28] Ana Rodriguez: hi all, quick note from procurement side, we'll need clear billing tiers and an amendment showing burst pricing, also any change to egress or license fees spelled out.
[00:40] Alex Mercer: totally. We can offer a 12-month retainer with a 20% burst buffer or a 6-month with dynamic burst; i'll send a pricing table after. Priya, can you walk through the performance trade-offs?
[00:55] Priya Kaur: sure. so main levers for your workload are batching vs latency, kv cache hit-rate and quantization profile. for Japan region we recommend dedicated reserved capacity to hit the latency SLOs, otherwise hosted with regional routing + caching can still meet most spikes but bursts may see 20-40ms uplift, depending.
[01:18] Sara Okoye: the team is sensitive to anything above 150ms tail p95, and for some API endpoints p99 matters. is that realistic?
[01:27] Priya Kaur: p95 150ms is feasible with dedicated nodes sized X and continuous batching tuned to your 60–80 req/s baseline. p99 is tougher but we can add an aggressive prefilling strategy + canary lane for high-priority flows. also note that kv cache helps a lot if your prompts have prefixes.
[01:46] Liam Chen: we've been experimenting with a smaller quantized model to cut cost, but concerned about hallucinations for critical outputs. any suggestions?
[01:53] Priya Kaur: common pattern—run quality-sensitive calls on full model in dedicated lane, lower-cost ones on quantized variant with a safety rerank. Redwood Optimize recommendations can suggest thresholds. we should also run evals on your key prompts.
[02:06] Michael Tran: about on-prem — for a handful of PII workloads we'd like a small on-prem pilot, VPC peering to your private control plane, and KMS/HSM integration. timeline is tight, target end of Q3.
[02:20] Alex Mercer: ok on-prem pilot is something we support; need to scope network and certs. our private offering supports KMS integrations and audit logs but procurement needs SOC2 addendum and a brief architecture diagram. i can get you a techpack.
[02:34] Ana Rodriguez: required: SOC 2 type 2 evidence, SSO/SAML flow diagram and details on data residency and log retention. also want to see how auth keys are rotated.
[02:46] Jonas Liu: we'll include the audit summary and key rotation policy. there might be a short lead time for HSM proofs depending on region.
[02:55] Sara Okoye: what about failover between EU and Japan? we need deterministic routing and an SLA for cross-region failover.
[03:02] Priya Kaur: routing is policy-driven; you can pin critical routes to Japan dedicated pool and set automated fallback to EU-dedicated nodes or a smaller hosted variant. failover adds ~30–70ms depending on cross-region hop but keeps service available. SLA can include latency targets and availability tiers, we'll bake that into the contract amendment.
[03:23] Liam Chen: cost — can you show the math for reserved vs hosted+burst? we need clarity for executive approval.
[03:30] Alex Mercer: yes i'll send a per-token and per-rt charge comparison. example: reserved nodes with 24/7 capacity vs hosted burst pricing; reserved has lower unit cost at commit but higher up-front. we can model your 6-month and 12-month scenarios.
[03:44] Michael Tran: for procurement's sake, can we get a consolidated doc with pricing, onboarding tasks, and a timeline including lead times for Japan region capacity?
[03:52] Alex Mercer: yes, that's next step.
[03:56] Priya Kaur: on the benchmark piece — can we run a targeted KV-cache and batching run? we'll need a sample prompt set, expected token lengths (avg 512), concurrency shape and p95/p99 goals.
[04:10] Michael Tran: i'll share a sample prompt corpus and traffic shape by EOD tomorrow.
[04:16] Ana Rodriguez: legal will want any contract amendment showing liabilities, termination clauses for the burst topup, and clear renewal triggers.
[04:26] Jonas Liu: noted. i'll flag our legal ops to prep an amendment template.
[04:30] Sara Okoye: one more — do you support IP allowlisting for the on-prem agent and can we enforce SSO for admin console?
[04:37] Alex Mercer: yes to both; IP allowlist and SSO (SAML) are supported in Private. We'll include steps for SSO setup in the techpack.
[04:44] Michael Tran: ok good.
[04:46] Alex Mercer: recap then, we will: send updated pricing with burst tiers, priya will run benchmarks once you share prompt set, we'll package SOC2 + KMS notes and an amendment draft, and schedule a pilot window for japan region. any objections?
[05:02] Ana Rodriguez: no objections, just need the docs to circulate to legal.
[05:06] Alex Mercer: perfect — thanks everyone. we'll follow up with a conda — sorry, con — i'll send calendar invites for the pilot and the benchmark sync.

Notes on transcription quality: occasional mis-words (e.g., 'conda' instead of 'calendar'), speaker overlap at several points. Natural speech patterns, interruptions, short crosstalk.
